title: Beginner Gamedev Logic & Variables
desc: Master player stats, damage calculations, boolean flags, and game loop timing.

guidebook.summary: Foundations of C# primitive types, arithmetic, condition branches, and for/while loops in game scripts.
tips: int stores whole numbers (health, ammo, gold) as 32-bit integers on the stack.
float stores fractional numbers (moveSpeed, timers, jumpForce) and needs an f suffix: 5.5f.
bool stores true/false flags for player state (isGrounded, isDead).
Time.deltaTime ensures movement speed is identical on 30 FPS and 144 FPS screens.

q.speech: Help me calculate the player's health after taking damage from a slime!
q.title: Basic HP Subtraction
q.instruction: What is printed to the Unity console?
q.summary: 100 minus 35 is 65! Primitive ints store direct numerical values on the stack.
q.analogy: Like subtracting hearts on your HUD when an enemy touches the collider.
q.memory: STACK: [maxHp = 100], [damage = 35], [currentHp = 65]

q.speech: Check if the game over screen triggers! Trace the boolean check.
q.title: Game Over Check
q.instruction: What will be output?
q.summary: playerHp <= 0 evaluates to true, so the if block executes.
q.analogy: Triggering the respawn menu as soon as health hits zero.
q.memory: isGameOver boolean is stored as a 1-byte true flag on the stack.

q.speech: How many enemies get spawned by this for-loop?
q.title: Enemy Spawner Loop
q.instruction: What is the final count of enemies spawned?
q.summary: i loops through 0, 1, 2, 3 (4 iterations total), incrementing enemiesSpawned to 4.
q.analogy: Spawning 4 zombies at wave start!
q.memory: i starts at 0, increments until i reaches 4.

q.speech: Why do we append 'f' to floating-point numbers in Unity C#?
q.title: Float Literal Syntax
q.instruction: Which line compiles without error for a float variable?
q.summary: In C#, bare decimal literals like 5.5 default to 64-bit double, requiring the f suffix for 32-bit float.
q.analogy: Speed in Unity uses 32-bit floats for fast hardware acceleration on mobile GPUs.
q.memory: 32-bit IEEE 754 float on stack vs 64-bit double.

q.speech: Can the character execute a double jump here?
q.title: Jump Condition Check
q.instruction: What is the boolean result of canJump?
q.summary: With || (OR), if either operand is true, the result is true. Since extraJumps > 0 is true, canJump is true.
q.analogy: Mid-air double-jumping when you still have a feather power-up active.
q.memory: Short-circuit evaluation: evaluates right side only when left is false.

q.speech: Watch out for infinite loops! How many potions are consumed?
q.title: While Loop Counter
q.instruction: What does this print?
q.summary: The while loop executes 3 times until potions reaches 0, incrementing drunk to 3.
q.analogy: Chugging healing potions one by one until your pouch is empty.
q.memory: potions decrements: 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 0; loop condition breaks at 0.

q.speech: Format our HUD string with modern C# string interpolation!
q.title: String Interpolation $""
q.instruction: Which syntax cleanly formats the player score into text?
q.code:
int score = 450;
// What gives: "Score: 450"?
q.summary: The $ prefix enables string interpolation, replacing {score} with its runtime value.
q.analogy: Printing player stats on the top UI banner dynamically.
q.memory: Compiles to String.Format or direct handler under the hood.

q.speech: Clean weapon state branching! Trace this switch statement.
q.title: Switch Expression
q.instruction: What damage value is assigned when weapon is "Bow"?
q.summary: The switch expression pattern matches "Bow" and returns 25.
q.analogy: Equipping an arrow that deals 25 ranged damage instead of dagger damage.
q.memory: Jump table / branch lookup generated by C# compiler.

q.speech: Array indices start at ZERO! What is ammo[1]?
q.title: Zero-Indexed Arrays
q.instruction: What value is stored at index 1?
q.code:
int[] ammo = new int[] { 30, 15, 6 };
Console.WriteLine(ammo[1]);
q.summary: Index 0 is 30, index 1 is 15, and index 2 is 6.
q.analogy: Slot 0 is Rifle ammo, Slot 1 is Shotgun shells (15).
q.memory: Fixed-size heap buffer: baseAddress + (1 * sizeof(int)).

q.speech: FINAL UNIT 1 BOSS TRIAL! Trace the full combat loop to defeat the gatekeeper!
q.title: Boss Health Loop
q.instruction: What is the final bossHp after 3 turns?
q.summary: 50 - (3 * 12) = 50 - 36 = 14! The boss has 14 HP remaining.
q.analogy: Striking a stone golem 3 times with a 12-power enchanted blade.
q.memory: Accumulator variable decremented in local stack frame.

title: Unity Engine Lifecycle & Architecture
desc: Awake, Start, Update, FixedUpdate, Time.deltaTime, and 3D vector movement.

guidebook.summary: Understanding when Unity calls your methods, frame rates, and game physics step.
tips: Awake() runs when the GameObject loads (initialize self references here).
Start() runs before the first frame update (initialize links to other objects here).
Update() runs once per graphical frame (handle user input and animations here).
FixedUpdate() runs at a constant physics interval (apply Rigidbody forces and velocities here).

q.speech: Why should you find components in Awake() rather than Start()?
q.title: Component Initialization Order
q.instruction: Which method is guaranteed to run BEFORE any other script Start() method?
q.summary: All Awake() calls across all active scripts finish before any Start() method is invoked.
q.analogy: Building all the stage props before the actors enter for opening night.
q.memory: Unity native C++ engine dispatches Awake pass across active scene components.

q.speech: I moved my Rigidbody inside Update() and it vibrated crazy! Where does physics belong?
q.title: Physics Stepping
q.instruction: Which Unity lifecycle method synchronizes with the PhysX simulation clock?
q.summary: FixedUpdate runs at a locked deterministic physics tick (default 50Hz, 0.02s).
q.analogy: Physics engine needs a steady metronome so balls bounce predictably.
q.memory: PhysX solver advances in discrete time steps decoupled from render FPS.

q.speech: Why does camera tracking code go into LateUpdate()?
q.title: Camera Tracking Jitter Prevention
q.instruction: What ensures the camera moves AFTER the player character has finished moving?
choices: LateUpdate executes after all Update() methods finish
LateUpdate runs on a separate GPU thread
LateUpdate runs only when camera stops
q.summary: LateUpdate() is called on every frame after all Update() functions have executed.
q.analogy: A film cameraman following the lead actor only after the actor takes their step.
q.memory: Unity engine loop queue: Input -> Update -> Physics -> LateUpdate -> Render.

q.speech: Without Time.deltaTime, my spaceship flies 10x faster on a gaming PC! Why?
q.title: Frame Rate Independence
q.instruction: What does Time.deltaTime represent in Unity?
q.code: transform.Translate(Vector3.forward * speed * Time.deltaTime);
choices: Elapsed seconds between current and previous frame
q.summary: Time.deltaTime is the fraction of a second that elapsed since the last render frame.
q.analogy: Multiplying by deltaTime converts speed from "units per frame" to "units per second".
q.memory: At 60 FPS, deltaTime is ~0.0166s. At 120 FPS, deltaTime is ~0.0083s.

q.speech: Calculate moving toward a target direction!
q.title: Direction Vector Formula
q.instruction: How do you calculate the direction vector from Player to Enemy?
q.code:
Vector3 playerPos = new Vector3(0, 0, 0);
Vector3 enemyPos = new Vector3(3, 0, 4);
q.summary: Target minus Origin gives the vector pointing from origin to target: (B - A).
q.analogy: Aiming an arrow from where you stand towards the monster.
q.memory: Component-wise subtraction: (3-0, 0-0, 4-0) = Vector3(3, 0, 4).

q.speech: In 2D games, which component handles velocity on a Rigidbody2D?
q.title: 2D Rigidbody Linear Velocity
q.instruction: How do you set velocity in Unity 2023+ / 6 for 2D movement?
q.code: rb2d.linearVelocity = moveInput * moveSpeed;
q.summary: rb2d.linearVelocity (formerly velocity) directly dictates unit movement per second.
q.analogy: Pushing the joystick in a top-down dungeon crawler like Zelda.
q.memory: Box2D physics solver updates position based on linearVelocity * fixedDeltaTime.

q.speech: TransformPoint converts local coordinates to what coordinate space?
q.title: Local to World Space Conversion
q.instruction: What does transform.TransformPoint(Vector3.forward) return?
q.code: Vector3 worldMuzzle = gunTransform.TransformPoint(Vector3.forward * 2f);
choices: World space coordinates relative to scene origin
q.summary: TransformPoint transforms position from local space to world space taking rotation into account.
q.analogy: Finding where the gun barrel tip is in the entire game world to spawn a muzzle flash.
q.memory: Multiplies local vector by GameObject 4x4 localToWorldMatrix.

q.speech: Why does Unity use Quaternions instead of Euler angles (x, y, z) for 3D rotations?
q.title: Gimbal Lock Prevention
q.instruction: What fatal mathematical flaw do Quaternions avoid?
q.code: transform.rotation = Quaternion.LookRotation(moveDirection);
choices: Gimbal Lock (loss of a degree of freedom)
Division by zero in CPU cache
q.summary: Euler angles suffer from Gimbal Lock when two rotational axes align. Quaternions (4D hypercomplex numbers) eliminate this completely.
q.analogy: Smoothly rotating an airplane nose without the compass spinning wildly.
q.memory: Stores 4 components (x, y, z, w) as a normalized 4D rotation sphere.

q.speech: What happens if you subscribe to an event in OnEnable but forget OnDisable?
q.title: Event Listener Ghost Leak
q.instruction: What critical bug occurs when you do not unsubscribe in OnDisable?
q.code:
void OnEnable() { GameManager.OnScoreChanged += UpdateScoreUI; }
void OnDisable() { GameManager.OnScoreChanged -= UpdateScoreUI; }
choices: Memory leak and MissingReferenceException when object is destroyed
q.summary: Static or publisher events retain a reference to your object, causing zombie callbacks after destruction.
q.analogy: Leaving your phone number on a company call list after you move out.
q.memory: Delegate invocation list retains strong reference preventing Garbage Collection.

lessons.title: Unit 2 Milestone Trial: Engine Master Trial

q.speech: CHALLENGE BOSS: Correctly order the Unity engine execution lifecycle from first to last!
q.title: Engine Lifecycle Sequence
q.instruction: Which sequence correctly matches the exact Unity event order?
q.code: // Choose the exact sequence of execution:
choices: Awake -> OnEnable -> Start -> FixedUpdate -> Update -> LateUpdate
q.summary: Awake runs first upon loading, then OnEnable, then Start, then FixedUpdate loop, Update, and LateUpdate.
q.analogy: The holy scriptures of the Unity Script Lifecycle flowchart!
q.memory: Native C++ dispatcher invokes managed method table in strict pipeline order.

title: Object-Oriented Gamedev & Memory Models
desc: Classes vs Structs, Heap vs Stack, Encapsulation, Polymorphism, and Interfaces.

guidebook.summary: Distinguish value types from reference types to eliminate memory aliasing bugs in game code.
tips: class is a reference type allocated on the Heap (variables hold memory addresses).
struct is a value type allocated on the Stack or inline (variables hold actual data).
Never use "new MonoBehaviour()"; always use AddComponent<T>() or Instantiate().
Interfaces like IDamageable allow swords, spells, and explosions to damage anything that can be hurt.

lessons.title: Classes vs Structs: Value vs Reference

q.speech: I copied player position into targetPos, modified targetPos, and player didn't move! Why?
q.title: Struct Value Copying
q.instruction: Because Vector3 is a struct (value type), what happens during assignment?
choices: 1 (a is unchanged, b is an independent copy)
q.summary: Structs are copied by value! Modifying b.x has zero effect on a.x.
q.analogy: Photocopying a quest map: drawing on your copy does not alter the original.
q.memory: Bitwise 12-byte copy on the stack frame (4 bytes for x, y, z each).

q.speech: BUG ALERT! Two goblins are sharing the same weapon stats object!
q.title: Class Reference Aliasing
q.instruction: What is printed when goblinA damages its weapon class?
choices: 20 (both variables point to the exact same Heap object)
q.summary: Classes are reference types! swordA and swordB hold references to the exact same Heap address.
q.analogy: Two players with shortcuts on their desktop pointing to the same server file.
q.memory: HEAP: [Weapon @ 0x8800 {durability: 20}]. STACK: swordA -> 0x8800, swordB -> 0x8800.

q.speech: How do you expose a variable in the Unity Inspector without making it public?
q.title: Encapsulation Best Practice
q.instruction: Which attribute exposes private variables safely to game designers?
q.code: [SerializeField] private float jumpForce = 12f;
q.summary: [SerializeField] tells Unity serializer to save the field and display it in Inspector while keeping it private.
q.analogy: Letting the level designer tweak jump height without letting other scripts mess with it.
q.memory: Unity YAML serializer reads private member via metadata reflection.

q.speech: Prevent player health from exceeding maxHealth using a C# property!
q.title: Property Clamping
q.instruction: What does this property ensure when healing?
choices: Health never goes below 0 or above 100
q.summary: The setter encapsulates logic, clamping incoming values within the allowed range.
q.analogy: A water bottle that overflows excess water instead of breaking.
q.memory: Property compiles into get_Health() and set_Health(int value) methods.

q.speech: What happens if a beginner writes 'PlayerController pc = new PlayerController();'?
q.title: MonoBehaviour Instantiation Rules
q.instruction: Why does Unity throw a warning when you use "new" on a MonoBehaviour?
q.code:
// WRONG: new PlayerMovement();
// RIGHT: gameObject.AddComponent<PlayerMovement>();
choices: MonoBehaviours require Unity native C++ GameObject bindings and lifecycle hooks
new is not a valid C# keyword
It takes too much stack memory
q.summary: MonoBehaviours are tied to GameObject transforms and native engine updates; they must be attached via AddComponent.
q.analogy: You cannot start an engine without bolting it inside a car chassis.
q.memory: Instantiate or AddComponent allocates the native C++ wrapper linked to managed C# peer.

q.speech: Code re-use in game architecture! Trace this class hierarchy.
q.title: Class Inheritance
q.instruction: Does Goblin have access to the TakeDamage method defined in Enemy?
choices: Yes, Goblin inherits all public and protected members of Enemy
No, Goblin must declare its own TakeDamage
Only if Enemy is an interface
q.summary: Subclasses inherit public and protected members of their parent base class.
q.analogy: All enemies take damage, but Goblins can also steal your gold!
q.memory: Goblin type descriptor inherits virtual method table (vtable) from Enemy.

q.speech: How do you allow a child enemy class to change how it attacks?
q.title: Polymorphism Keywords
q.instruction: Which keywords enable dynamic method overriding in C#?
choices: virtual in base class, override in child class
static in base class, const in child class
abstract in base, sealed in child
interface in base, struct in child
q.summary: virtual marks a method as overrideable; override replaces the implementation in the derived class.
q.analogy: Standard monsters punch, but Dragon bosses breathe fire when Attack() is called!
q.memory: VTable slot for Attack points to MageEnemy.Attack at runtime.

q.speech: Can you instantiate an abstract class directly?
q.title: Abstract Class Blueprint
q.instruction: Can you call new BaseWeapon() if BaseWeapon is declared abstract?
choices: No, abstract classes cannot be instantiated, only inherited
Yes, if it has a constructor
q.summary: Abstract classes serve as blueprints and require concrete derived classes to implement abstract members.
q.analogy: You cannot hold an "abstract weapon" in your hand; you hold a Pistol or Shotgun.
q.memory: Compiler rejects direct instantiation of incomplete type descriptors.

q.speech: Why use an IDamageable interface instead of checking 'if (target is Enemy)'?
q.title: Interface Decoupling
q.instruction: What is the main architectural benefit of an IDamageable interface?
choices: Any entity (Enemy, Wooden Crate, Exploding Barrel) can take damage without code coupling
Interfaces save battery on mobile devices
q.summary: Interfaces allow unrelated classes to implement a common contract, decoupling weapons from target types.
q.analogy: Your rocket launcher damages tanks, zombies, and wooden doors with the same code!
q.memory: Interface dispatch uses interface vtable (itable) lookup.

q.speech: OOP ARCHITECTURE TRIAL! What is output when we iterate through damageables?
q.title: Polymorphic Interface Loop
q.instruction: What gets executed when bullet hits targets via IDamageable?
choices: Each target executes its own specific TakeDamage implementation
q.summary: Polymorphism allows treating different types uniformly through their shared interface contract.
q.analogy: The game world treats anything destructible with one elegant line of code.
q.memory: Dynamic dispatch via itable resolves the appropriate TakeDamage method address.

title: Game Math, 3D Physics & Collisions
desc: Rigidbodies, Colliders, Raycasts, Dot Product vision cones, and Vector Math.

guidebook.summary: Harness Unity physics simulation and 3D vector geometry for combat, movement, and collisions.
tips: Use ForceMode.Impulse for instant explosive forces (jumping, cannon shot).
Use ForceMode.Force for continuous acceleration (jetpack thrust).
Vector3.Dot gives positive values when facing the same direction, negative when facing away.
Use Physics.Raycast with a LayerMask so bullets do not collide with the player shooting them.

q.speech: Which ForceMode should we use when the hero jumps?
q.title: Instant Impulse Force
q.instruction: Which ForceMode applies an instantaneous change in momentum using mass?
q.code: rb.AddForce(Vector3.up * jumpForce, ForceMode.Impulse);
q.summary: ForceMode.Impulse applies an instant force taking mass into account, perfect for jumps and explosions.
q.analogy: A sudden spring releasing under your boots to vault you upward.
q.memory: Directly adjusts Rigidbody momentum vector: deltaV = impulse / mass.

q.speech: Why didn't my player pick up the coin when walking into it?
q.title: Trigger Collider Setup
q.instruction: To detect overlaps without causing a physical solid collision, what checkbox must be checked on the Collider?
q.summary: Is Trigger turns off physical solid collision response and triggers OnTriggerEnter/Stay/Exit callbacks.
q.analogy: Walking through a ghost doorway that counts your visit without stubbing your toe.
q.memory: PhysX broadphase logs overlap event without generating contact manifolds or solver forces.

q.speech: Shoot a laser from the player's eyes forward! What does Physics.Raycast return?
q.title: Raycast Boolean Return
q.instruction: What is the return type of Physics.Raycast?
q.code: bool hasHit = Physics.Raycast(transform.position, transform.forward, out RaycastHit hit, 100f);
choices: bool (true if the ray intersected any matching collider)
q.summary: Physics.Raycast returns a bool indicating whether a collider was hit; details are stored in the out hit parameter.
q.analogy: Shooting an invisible laser pointer: either the red dot hits a wall or it travels into the sky.
q.memory: PhysX spatial bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) traversal test.

q.speech: We want bullets to ricochet off metal walls! Which property of RaycastHit gives the surface tilt?
q.title: Surface Normal Vector
q.instruction: Which vector is perpendicular to the hit surface?
q.code: Vector3 reflectDir = Vector3.Reflect(bulletDir, hit.normal);
q.summary: hit.normal is a unit vector perpendicular to the triangle surface where the ray intersected.
q.analogy: Like an arrow pointing straight out of a wall at a 90 degree angle.
q.memory: Interpolated normal vector from polygon mesh contact plane.

q.speech: Prevent raycasts from hitting your own player collider!
q.title: LayerMask Bitshift
q.instruction: How do you create a LayerMask integer for the "Enemy" layer (layer index 8)?
q.code: int layerMask = 1 << LayerMask.NameToLayer("Enemy");
q.summary: Bit shifting 1 << layerIndex produces a 32-bit bitmask where only bit 8 is turned on (value 256).
q.analogy: Wearing night-vision goggles tuned strictly to the frequency of enemy heat signatures.
q.memory: 32-bit integer bitwise AND filter used in PhysX collision pipeline.

q.speech: PRO OPTIMIZATION! Checking distances between 500 enemies every frame!
q.title: Square Distance Optimization
q.instruction: Why is (a - b).sqrMagnitude faster than Vector3.Distance(a, b)?
q.code:
float distSqr = (enemy.position - player.position).sqrMagnitude;
if (distSqr < range * range) { /* In range! */ }
choices: It avoids calculating an expensive square root (Mathf.Sqrt)
It runs on the audio processor
q.summary: Square root calculations are slow on CPUs. Comparing squared distance to squared range yields the exact same result without sqrt!
q.analogy: Testing if x^2 + y^2 < 25 instead of calculating sqrt(x^2 + y^2) < 5.
q.memory: Eliminates dozens of CPU floating-point sqrt instruction cycles per frame.

q.speech: Can the guard see the sneaking thief?
q.title: Vector3.Dot Vision Cone
q.instruction: When Vector3.Dot(guardForward, dirToThief) is greater than 0, where is the thief?
q.code:
float dot = Vector3.Dot(guard.forward, dirToThief);
bool inFront = dot > 0f;
choices: In front of the guard (angle < 90 degrees)
q.summary: The Dot product of two normalized vectors equals cos(angle). If dot > 0, the target is in the front 180-degree hemisphere.
q.analogy: A guard cone of sight: if dot > 0.707, they are within a 90-degree forward vision cone!
q.memory: Calculation: (ax*bx + ay*by + az*bz).

q.speech: Find the rotational axis when steering a tank along a hillside!
q.title: Cross Product Direction
q.instruction: What is the geometric relationship of Vector3.Cross(A, B) to vectors A and B?
q.code: Vector3 torqueAxis = Vector3.Cross(transform.forward, slopeNormal);
choices: Perpendicular (orthogonal) to both vectors A and B
Sum of lengths of A and B
q.summary: The Cross product produces a vector that is perpendicular to both input vectors (right-hand rule).
q.analogy: The axle of a spinning wheel is perpendicular to both its spokes and its direction of travel.
q.memory: Determinant cross-multiplication: (ay*bz - az*by, az*bx - ax*bz, ax*by - ay*bx).

q.speech: Smoothly glide a health bar fill amount!
q.title: Linear Interpolation (Lerp)
q.instruction: What does Mathf.Lerp(0f, 100f, 0.5f) return?
q.code: float current = Mathf.Lerp(0f, 100f, 0.5f);
q.summary: Mathf.Lerp(a, b, t) calculates a + (b - a) * t. At t = 0.5f, it is exactly halfway (50f).
q.analogy: Sliding a dimmer switch halfway between pitch black (0) and maximum brightness (100).
q.memory: Single multiply-add floating point operation.

q.speech: PHYSICS MILESTONE BOSS! Find the error in this ground-check raycast script!
q.title: Ground Check Raycast Bug
q.instruction: Why did the character fail to jump when standing on the ground?
q.code:
// Ground check attempt:
bool isGrounded = Physics.Raycast(transform.position, Vector3.up, 1.1f);
choices: The ray was cast Vector3.up instead of Vector3.down!
q.summary: Vector3.up casts into the sky! Ground checks must cast downwards (Vector3.down or -transform.up).
q.analogy: Looking at the ceiling to check if your feet are touching the floor!
q.memory: Ray direction vector (0, 1, 0) points away from ground plane.

title: Collections, Data Structures & Inventory
desc: Lists, Dictionaries, HashSets, Queues, Stacks, 2D Grids, and GC-safe iterations.

guidebook.summary: Pick the optimal collection for your game systems: O(1) lookups with Dictionaries, fast queues, and avoiding GC garbage.
tips: List<T> is great for dynamic collections, but resizing copies the internal array.
Dictionary<TKey, TValue> provides near O(1) lookups by item ID or name.
Queue<T> provides FIFO (First-In, First-Out) queuing for combat action buffers.
Avoid LINQ statements (.Where, .ToList) inside 60fps Update loops to prevent GC frame stutters.

q.speech: Add loot drops into player bag!
q.title: List Add & Count
q.instruction: What is items.Count after this code executes?
q.summary: Adding two items and removing one leaves exactly 1 item in the list.
q.analogy: Picking up a key, opening a dungeon gate (consuming the key), leaving only your potion.
q.memory: Internal array shifts elements; Count property decrements.

q.speech: Instant item lookup without searching through 1,000 array elements!
q.title: Dictionary O(1) Speed
q.instruction: What is the average time complexity of finding a value in a Dictionary by Key?
q.summary: Dictionaries use hash tables to jump directly to the memory bucket for the key in O(1) time.
q.analogy: Opening a dictionary directly to letter "S" instead of reading every word from page 1.
q.memory: Key string gets hashed via GetHashCode() mapping to bucket array index.

q.speech: Check if the player has unlocked Quest 42 without duplicates!
q.title: HashSet Uniqueness & Lookup
q.instruction: What happens if you Add(42) twice to a HashSet<int>?
choices: 1 (HashSets guarantee unique elements and ignore duplicate adds)
q.summary: HashSets store unique elements; adding an existing item returns false and does nothing.
q.analogy: A trophy case: you can only display one gold medal for each unique achievement.
q.memory: Bucket collision resolves to existing entry; no reallocation occurs.

q.speech: Buffer player attack inputs in a fighting game!
q.title: FIFO Queue Processing
q.instruction: In what order are actions dequeued from a Queue<T>?
q.summary: Queues process items in First-In First-Out order (FIFO).
q.analogy: Standing in line at the theater box office: the first person in line gets tickets first.
q.memory: Circular ring buffer with head and tail pointers.

q.speech: Pressing the ESC button should close the top-most menu modal!
q.title: LIFO Stack Navigation
q.instruction: In what order are elements popped from a Stack<T>?
q.summary: Stacks follow Last-In First-Out (LIFO). The most recently pushed menu is popped first.
q.analogy: A stack of dinner plates: you always grab the plate on top.
q.memory: Pointer to top element decrements on pop; zero heap allocations when within capacity.

q.speech: Map grid tile [x, y] coordinates to world positions!
q.title: Tilemap Grid Formula
q.instruction: If each grid cell is 2.0 units wide, what is the world position for cell [3, 4]?
q.summary: 3 * 2 = 6 and 4 * 2 = 8, yielding Vector3(6, 0, 8).
q.analogy: Chess board coordinates: each square is spaced by an exact tile dimension.
q.memory: Continuous flat memory array stride: index = x + y * gridWidth.

q.speech: Why should you NOT use 'enemies.Where(e => e.hp > 0).ToList()' inside Update()?
q.title: LINQ Garbage Collector Hitching
q.instruction: What is the danger of running LINQ expressions every frame?
q.code:
// RUNNING IN UPDATE() EVERY FRAME:
var alive = enemies.Where(e => e.hp > 0).ToList();
choices: Allocates temporary objects on the Heap, triggering GC spikes and frame drops
LINQ makes game characters run backwards
q.summary: LINQ statements allocate iterators, delegate closures, and new List instances on the heap every frame.
q.analogy: Tossing plastic wrappers on the floor 60 times a second until the cleaning crew halts everything to sweep.
q.memory: Heap churn pushes GC into Gen0 collection pause during gameplay.

q.speech: A character can be BOTH Poisoned AND Frozen at the same time!
q.title: Bitmask Enum Flags
q.instruction: Which attribute and operator combines multiple enum values into one variable?
q.summary: [Flags] enables bitwise combination (|) and checking ((current & Status.Poisoned) != 0).
q.analogy: Stacking debuff icons over a hero head in an RPG.
q.memory: Stored as binary bits in a single byte: 0001 | 0010 = 0011 (value 3).

q.speech: Why is GetComponent<Rigidbody>() safer than older GetComponent(string name)?
q.title: Compile-Time Type Safety
q.instruction: What major advantage do C# Generics (<T>) provide?
q.code: Rigidbody rb = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
choices: Compile-time type checking and no string typo bugs or explicit casting
q.summary: Generics provide strong compile-time type safety, avoiding runtime string searches and cast exceptions.
q.analogy: A custom tool slot that only accepts a 10mm wrench instead of guessing tool names.
q.memory: C# JIT compiler generates specialized native method call for the specific type token.

q.speech: DATA STRUCTURES BOSS! Choose the right collection for an enemy lookup by unique ID!
q.title: Optimal Collection Choice
q.instruction: Which data structure finds an enemy by unique integer ID in O(1) time with no duplicates?
q.code: // Choose collection for: GetEnemyById(int id)
q.summary: Dictionary<int, Enemy> maps IDs directly to Enemy instances in O(1) constant time.
q.analogy: Looking up a hotel guest room number directly from their room card key.
q.memory: Internal bucket array indexed by hash mod size.

title: Events, Delegates & Decoupled Architecture
desc: Delegates, Actions, Funcs, Events, Observer Pattern, and Global Event Buses.

guidebook.summary: Decouple game systems so player scripts do not need references to UI, Audio, or Camera managers.
tips: Use Action for callbacks that return void (e.g. Action<int> onTakeDamage).
Use Func for callbacks that return a value (e.g. Func<int, float> getMultiplier).
Always unsubscribe in OnDisable (-=) to prevent ghost listener memory leaks.
The Observer Pattern lets UI and Audio listen to gameplay without player scripts knowing they exist.

q.speech: What is a delegate in C#?
q.title: Delegate Definition
q.instruction: What does a delegate variable actually store?
q.code:
public delegate void AttackCallback(int damage);
AttackCallback onAttack = Punch;
choices: A type-safe reference to a method (function pointer)
q.summary: A delegate is a type-safe object that holds references to one or more methods with matching signatures.
q.analogy: A walkie-talkie channel where someone broadcasts an alert to listening listeners.
q.memory: MulticastDelegate object on heap with _target (object) and _methodPtr (pointer).

q.speech: Stop writing custom delegate definitions! Use System.Action!
q.title: System.Action Signature
q.instruction: What return type does System.Action always have?
q.code: public System.Action<int> OnCoinsChanged;
choices: void (it does not return a value)
q.summary: System.Action delegates represent methods that return void. Action<int> takes one int parameter.
q.analogy: A megaphone announcement that announces news without expecting an answer back.
q.memory: Standard library delegate definition: public delegate void Action<T>(T obj).

q.speech: What is the difference between Action and Func in C#?
q.title: Func Return Value
q.instruction: Which parameter represents the return type in Func<int, int, bool>?
q.code:
System.Func<int, int, bool> isCriticalHit;
// (atk, defense) => bool
choices: bool (the LAST type argument is always the return type)
q.summary: In System.Func, the final generic type parameter is always the return type.
q.analogy: Asking an appraiser how much a gem is worth: they inspect it and return the value.
q.memory: Compiler expands to: public delegate TResult Func<in T1, in T2, out TResult>.

q.speech: Why add the 'event' keyword before an Action?
q.title: Event Protection Keyword
q.instruction: What illegal operation does the "event" keyword prevent other scripts from doing?
q.code: public static event Action OnPlayerDied;
choices: Prevents outside classes from invoking or clearing (= null) the event
q.summary: The event keyword restricts outside classes to only subscribing (+=) and unsubscribing (-=).
q.analogy: Only the radio station host can broadcast; listeners can only tune in, not hijack the mic.
q.memory: Compiler generates private backing field and public add/remove accessor methods.

q.speech: The player died, the level reloaded, but old UI scripts kept triggering! Why?
q.title: Unsubscribe with -=
q.instruction: Which operator removes your method from an event listener list?
q.summary: The -= operator removes the delegate handler, allowing the object to be cleanly garbage collected.
q.analogy: Cancelling your magazine subscription when you move houses so mail stops arriving.
q.memory: Delegate.Remove creates a new invocation list without the target reference.

q.speech: When should you use UnityEvent instead of C# Action?
q.title: UnityEvent Inspector Hookup
q.instruction: What is the main benefit of UnityEvent over pure C# Action?
q.code: [SerializeField] public UnityEngine.Events.UnityEvent onChestOpened;
choices: It can be wired up visually in the Unity Inspector by level designers
It runs 100x faster than C# Actions
It works without any C# scripts
q.summary: UnityEvent allows designers to drag and drop GameObjects and hook up method calls in the Editor.
q.analogy: Plugging an audio cable into an amplifier in the physical studio without soldering wires.
q.memory: Uses reflection and serialized persistent call list; slightly more overhead than C# Action.

q.speech: Should the PlayerHealth script have a 'public HealthBarUI ui' reference?
q.title: Decoupled Observer Pattern
q.instruction: Why is it cleaner for HealthBarUI to observe PlayerHealth than PlayerHealth owning HealthBarUI?
q.code:
// PlayerHealth has NO references to UI:
OnHealthChanged?.Invoke(currentHealth);
choices: PlayerHealth can run in test scenes with NO UI present without throwing null errors
q.summary: Decoupling ensures the gameplay logic functions independently of whether a UI or audio listener exists.
q.analogy: A rock band plays music whether 10 people or 10,000 people are listening in the crowd.
q.memory: Zero coupling: PlayerHealth holds no pointer to HealthBarUI object.

q.speech: Play a jump sound effect without referencing AudioManager in PlayerController!
q.title: Audio Event Trigger
q.instruction: How can the sound play cleanly through an event?
choices: Player triggers event; AudioManager listens and plays sound
Player plays sound on CPU directly
Unity handles it automatically with no code
q.summary: The player script emits the event; the audio system listens and responds without direct coupling.
q.analogy: Pulling the fire alarm: the alarm system handles sirens without the person shouting.
q.memory: Static event dispatches to all registered listeners in invoke queue.

q.speech: What is a Global Event Bus in game architecture?
q.title: Event Bus Pattern
q.instruction: What role does an EventBus class play in large game projects?
q.code: EventBus.Publish(new EnemyDefeatedEvent(enemyId, xpAwarded));
choices: A centralized messaging hub that dispatches events across disconnected systems
A bus vehicle model in Unity physics
q.summary: An Event Bus acts as a central hub where publishers post events and subscribers listen by event type.
q.analogy: The post office: anyone can drop off mail, and the post office delivers it to whoever subscribed.
q.memory: Type-keyed dictionary mapping EventType -> Action<TEvent>.

lessons.title: Unit 6 Milestone Trial: Event Bus Gauntlet

q.speech: EVENTS MILESTONE BOSS! What does '?.' (null-conditional) do before .Invoke()?
q.title: Null-Conditional Event Invocation
q.instruction: Why do we write OnScoreChanged?.Invoke(score)?
q.code: OnScoreChanged?.Invoke(score);
choices: It checks if OnScoreChanged has any subscribers before invoking, preventing NullReferenceException
It delays the call by 1 frame
It converts score to a float
q.summary: If no scripts subscribed to the event, OnScoreChanged is null. The ?. operator safely prevents a crash.
q.analogy: Checking if anyone is on the other end of the telephone before speaking.
q.memory: Thread-safe copy and null check before CALLVIRT instruction.

title: Coroutines, Timers & Asynchronous Systems
desc: IEnumerator, yield return, WaitForSeconds, UniTask, and Async/Await in game loops.

guidebook.summary: Execute logic across multiple frames without freezing the game UI using Coroutines and Tasks.
tips: Coroutines execute up to a "yield return", then pause until the engine resumes them next frame.
Use WaitForSecondsRealtime() if a timer needs to run while the game is paused (Time.timeScale = 0).
Store your Coroutine reference so you can call StopCoroutine() safely when interrupted.
UniTask provides zero-allocation async/await tailored for Unity performance.

q.speech: Why can't we use Thread.Sleep(3000) to wait 3 seconds in a game?
q.title: Main Thread Freezing
q.instruction: What catastrophe happens if you call Thread.Sleep() on Unity main thread?
q.code:
// WRONG: Thread.Sleep(3000);
// RIGHT: StartCoroutine(WaitRoutine());
choices: The entire game freezes completely, dropping to 0 FPS for 3 seconds
q.summary: Thread.Sleep halts the main thread that renders graphics, freezing the entire window.
q.analogy: Freezing time in the universe instead of just waiting for an egg timer to ding.
q.memory: Blocks OS main message loop and DirectX swapchain present call.

q.speech: How do you pause a coroutine for exactly ONE frame?
q.title: Single Frame Yield
q.instruction: Which yield statement waits for the very next frame to continue?
q.summary: yield return null pauses execution and resumes on the very next frame.
q.analogy: Taking a breath between sword swings and continuing on the next frame tick.
q.memory: Coroutine manager queues the IEnumerator for MoveNext() in next frame update pass.

q.speech: When the game is paused (Time.timeScale = 0), which yield instruction still works?
q.title: Unscaled Realtime Timers
q.instruction: Why does yield return new WaitForSeconds(1f) freeze indefinitely when timeScale is 0?
q.code:
// Pause Menu Animation:
yield return new WaitForSecondsRealtime(1.5f);
choices: WaitForSeconds relies on scaled time (timeScale = 0 means 0 seconds pass); WaitForSecondsRealtime uses system clock
q.summary: WaitForSeconds scales with Time.timeScale. When paused, use WaitForSecondsRealtime.
q.analogy: Your wristwatch continues ticking even if you hit the pause button on your DVD player.
q.memory: Reads unscaled real-time hardware clock (System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch).

q.speech: The player died while drinking a potion! Cancel the potion coroutine immediately!
q.title: Coroutine Handle Cancellation
q.instruction: How do you store and cancel a specific running coroutine?
choices: Store the Coroutine handle and pass it to StopCoroutine()
q.summary: Passing the stored Coroutine handle stops only that specific routine without killing other scripts.
q.analogy: Tearing up one specific ticket rather than evicting everyone from the stadium.
q.memory: Unity engine removes specific coroutine node from active linked list.

q.speech: Smooth screen fade out to black over 2 seconds!
q.title: Fade Loop Pattern
q.instruction: What loop condition ensures the fade lasts exactly duration seconds?
choices: while (t < duration) with t += Time.deltaTime and yield return null
for (int i=0; i<100; i++) with Thread.Sleep
q.summary: Accumulating deltaTime each frame while t < duration produces a smooth time-based transition.
q.analogy: Gradually sliding a fader up from 0% opacity to 100% opacity over 2 seconds.
q.memory: Normalized parameter (t / duration) goes smoothly from 0.0 to 1.0.

lessons.title: Async / Await in Modern Unity C#

q.speech: Can we use standard C# 'async Task' methods in modern Unity?
q.title: Task vs Coroutine Return
q.instruction: What is a major advantage of async Tasks over Coroutines?
choices: Tasks can return values (e.g. Task<int>) directly, whereas Coroutines cannot
Tasks only work in offline games
q.summary: Async methods can easily return typed values (Task<T>) and handle try/catch exceptions cleanly.
q.analogy: Ordering food at a counter and receiving your meal tray when your number is called.
q.memory: State machine struct generated by compiler with AsyncTaskMethodBuilder.

q.speech: Why do top mobile game studios use UniTask instead of System.Threading.Tasks?
q.title: UniTask Zero-Allocation
q.instruction: What is the primary performance benefit of UniTask in game loops?
q.code: await UniTask.Delay(1000, ignoreTimeScale: false);
choices: UniTask uses value-type structs that generate zero GC allocations on await
UniTask runs on the GPU rasterizer
q.summary: Standard Task generates heap allocations for every task object; UniTask is struct-based and zero-allocation.
q.analogy: Renting a reusable metal tray instead of throwing away paper cups on every order.
q.memory: Struct UniTask avoids GC Gen0 heap pressure.

q.speech: Prevent an async task from modifying a destroyed GameObject after level restart!
q.title: CancellationToken Protection
q.instruction: Which Unity helper token automatically cancels when the GameObject is destroyed?
q.code: await UniTask.Delay(5000, cancellationToken: this.GetCancellationTokenOnDestroy());
q.summary: Binding the task to the destruction token aborts execution if the scene reloads, preventing null errors.
q.analogy: Cancelling your pizza order if you move away before it arrives.
q.memory: OperationCanceledException safely caught and short-circuited.

q.speech: Display a 0% to 100% loading bar while loading the Next Dungeon Level!
q.title: AsyncOperation Progress
q.instruction: Which API loads a scene in the background without freezing gameplay?
q.summary: LoadSceneAsync loads assets in the background, reporting op.progress (0.0 to 0.9) until activation.
q.analogy: A backstage crew building the next scene behind the curtains while actors finish talking.
q.memory: Background asset streaming thread deserializes serialized files into memory.

lessons.title: Unit 7 Milestone Trial: Time Bender Challenge

q.speech: ASYNC MILESTONE BOSS! What does 'yield break;' do inside a Coroutine?
q.title: Yield Break Immediate Exit
q.instruction: What is the effect of calling yield break;?
choices: Immediately terminates the coroutine execution permanently
q.summary: yield break immediately halts the coroutine, signaling MoveNext() has no further iterations.
q.analogy: Hanging up the phone call immediately because the party left.
q.memory: MoveNext() returns false; engine removes routine from active runner pool.

title: ScriptableObjects & Data-Driven Architecture
desc: Asset menus, modular weapon stats, ScriptableObject events, and runtime sets.

guidebook.summary: Store data in project assets rather than scene instances to share stats, reduce memory, and build modular systems.
tips: [CreateAssetMenu] allows you to right-click in Project folder to create new data assets.
ScriptableObjects do not store transform or scene data, making them lightweight.
Use ScriptableObject Game Events to create ultra-decoupled architecture (Ryan Hipple pattern).
Runtime Sets automatically register active enemies on Awake and unregister on Destroy.

q.speech: How do you allow designers to right-click in the Project window and create a new Item data file?
q.title: CreateAssetMenu Attribute
q.instruction: Which attribute exposes the asset creation option in the Unity menu?
q.summary: [CreateAssetMenu] adds your custom ScriptableObject to the Assets -> Create context menu.
q.analogy: Creating a new template card in your trading card binder.
q.memory: Creates a .asset YAML file in the project directory.

q.speech: Why should 100 goblin prefabs all reference ONE GoblinStats ScriptableObject?
q.title: Memory Flyweight Sharing
q.instruction: What is the architectural advantage of referencing a shared ScriptableObject for stats?
choices: All 100 goblins share the exact same stats memory, and tweaking the asset updates all goblins live
q.summary: Sharing a ScriptableObject avoids duplicating stats data across hundreds of instances and allows live balance tuning.
q.analogy: All soldiers in an army reading from the same field manual instead of printing 10,000 separate rulebooks.
q.memory: Single heap instance loaded in memory; instances store only a pointer to it.

q.speech: The famous Ryan Hipple Unite talk: Game Events as Assets!
q.title: ScriptableObject Event Channel
q.instruction: Where does a ScriptableObject GameEvent live in your Unity project?
choices: In the Project folder as an independent .asset file
Inside scene Hierarchy attached to Camera
q.summary: Event assets exist in the Project folder, allowing scenes to communicate without direct references.
q.analogy: A shared public bulletin board where anyone can pin a notice and anyone can read it.
q.memory: Project asset persists across scene unloads without DontDestroyOnLoad.

q.speech: Find all active enemies without calling GameObject.FindGameObjectsWithTag('Enemy')!
q.title: Runtime Set Auto-Registration
q.instruction: How does an Enemy register itself into a ScriptableObject RuntimeSet?
choices: Enemies add themselves in OnEnable and remove in OnDisable
q.summary: Self-registering runtime sets give you an instant list of active enemies with zero search overhead.
q.analogy: Checking in at the gym reception desk when you arrive, and checking out when you leave.
q.memory: O(1) list insertion; no expensive scene hierarchy scans.

q.speech: Randomize footsteps audio with slight pitch variance!
q.title: Audio SO Configuration
q.instruction: How does an AudioEvent asset prevent repetitive machine-gun audio clicks?
choices: It picks random audio clips and randomizes pitch in a narrow range
q.summary: Randomizing clip selection and pitch creates natural, organic sound effects.
q.analogy: Every footstep crunching in the snow sounds subtly different.
q.memory: Lightweight configuration struct applied to audio hardware voice.

q.speech: Design branching NPC dialogue without messy nested switch statements!
q.title: Dialogue Node Data Asset
q.instruction: How do dialogue nodes link to follow-up responses in ScriptableObjects?
choices: Each choice holds a reference to the next DialogueNode ScriptableObject
By searching line numbers in text
q.summary: Node assets reference child nodes, forming an editable branching graph in the editor.
q.analogy: A "Choose Your Own Adventure" book: "If you open the chest, turn to Node 12".
q.memory: Graph data structure serialized into YAML asset files.

q.speech: Equip a 'Fire Enchantment' buff to our sword!
q.title: Modular Buff Asset
q.instruction: Why is defining buffs as ScriptableObjects better than writing 50 if-statements in Weapon?
choices: You can create new buffs by just making new assets without modifying the core Weapon code
q.summary: Open-Closed Principle: Open for extension (new buff assets), closed for modification (Weapon script unchanged).
q.analogy: Slotting different elemental gems into the hilt of your sword.
q.memory: Polymorphic dispatch over buff asset array.

q.speech: Tweak zombie patrol speed across 20 scenes at once!
q.title: Global Balance Tuning
q.instruction: If you change patrolSpeed in ZombieConfig.asset, which zombies receive the update?
q.code: [SerializeField] private AIConfig zombieConfig;
choices: Every zombie referencing that config across all scenes and prefabs
Only the first zombie in the hierarchy
Only zombies in the active camera view
q.summary: Because the asset is shared, editing it updates every prefab and instance that points to it.
q.analogy: Updating the rulebook in the head office instantly updates every branch store.
q.memory: Single source of truth in project memory cache.

q.speech: Save the player's inventory to disk so they can quit and resume tomorrow!
q.title: JsonUtility Serialization
q.instruction: Which Unity utility serializes a C# data object into a JSON string?
q.code:
string json = JsonUtility.ToJson(saveData, prettyPrint: true);
File.WriteAllText(savePath, json);
q.summary: JsonUtility.ToJson converts supported C# data structures into clean human-readable JSON strings.
q.analogy: Writing down your character stats onto a parchment save-file before closing the game.
q.memory: Fast native C++ serializer traverses marked [Serializable] fields.

q.speech: DATA ARCHITECTURE BOSS! What happens to modified ScriptableObject variables during Play Mode in the Unity Editor?
q.title: Editor ScriptableObject State Persistence Trap
q.instruction: In the Unity Editor, if a script modifies a ScriptableObject variable during Play Mode, what happens when you exit Play Mode?
q.code:
// Tweak during Play Mode:
statsAsset.health -= 10;
choices: The changes persist in the Editor asset on disk (unlike MonoBehaviours which reset)!
q.summary: In the Unity Editor, ScriptableObject modifications persist across play sessions! Always reset runtime state or use non-destructive copies.
q.analogy: Drawing in permanent marker on your master blueprint instead of using a dry-erase marker.
q.memory: Editor asset file dirty flag marks changes into project memory representation.

title: Scalable Game Design Patterns
desc: Singletons, State Machines, Object Pools, Command Pattern, and Factory Pattern.

guidebook.summary: Professional architecture patterns used by AAA and top indie teams to build scalable, bug-free game engines.
tips: Object Pooling reuses destroyed projectiles and particles to eliminate GC allocation hitches.
Finite State Machines (FSM) keep enemy AI states (Idle, Chase, Attack) clean and organized.
Singletons should be used sparingly for core managers (Audio, Save, GameController).
Command Pattern encapsulates player actions for easy input rebinding and replay systems.

q.speech: Access GameManager.Instance from anywhere in the game!
q.title: Singleton Pattern Implementation
q.instruction: What pattern ensures only ONE instance of a class exists globally?
q.summary: The Singleton pattern provides a global access point to a single instance while destroying duplicate spawns.
q.analogy: There can be only one President of the country at any given time.
q.memory: Static reference in type table pointing to the solitary active instance on the heap.

q.speech: Keep the AudioManager alive when loading from Main Menu into Level 1!
q.title: DontDestroyOnLoad Persistence
q.instruction: Which Unity API keeps a GameObject alive across scene transitions?
q.code: DontDestroyOnLoad(gameObject);
q.summary: DontDestroyOnLoad moves the GameObject into a special DontDestroyOnLoad scene that never unloads.
q.analogy: A backpack you carry through every room in a castle without leaving it behind.
q.memory: Native engine moves transform root to the persistent scene manager list.

q.speech: Clean enemy AI without 50 nested if-else statements!
q.title: FSM Interface
q.instruction: What interface methods define a classic state in a Finite State Machine?
q.summary: Enter handles state setup, Update handles frame logic, and Exit handles state cleanup before transitioning.
q.analogy: Traffic lights: Green (Enter), Green timer (Update), Turn off Green (Exit) -> Yellow (Enter).
q.memory: Polymorphic state reference currentState.Update() executes active state logic.

q.speech: Enable player input rebinding and action replay/undo!
q.title: Command Pattern Execution
q.instruction: What does the Command Pattern encapsulate?
choices: An action or request as a standalone object with Execute() and Undo()
q.summary: The Command pattern encapsulates requests as objects, allowing action queuing, logging, and undo/redo.
q.analogy: A restaurant order slip: the waiter hands the chef a ticket that can be prepared or refunded.
q.memory: Command instances stored in history stack for execution and reversal.

q.speech: Shooting 50 machine gun bullets per second without lagging the game!
q.title: Object Pooling Concept
q.instruction: Instead of calling Instantiate() and Destroy(), what does an Object Pool do?
q.code:
// WRONG: Destroy(bullet);
// RIGHT: bullet.SetActive(false); pool.Return(bullet);
choices: Deactivates bullets and reuses them from a pre-warmed queue
q.summary: Object Pooling recycles inactive objects, completely eliminating Instantiate and Destroy GC overhead.
q.analogy: Borrowing bowling shoes at the alley: you return them to the counter for the next customer.
q.memory: Zero heap allocations at runtime; stable memory footprint prevents GC pauses.

q.speech: Reset bullet velocities when spawning from the pool!
q.title: IPoolable Reset Interface
q.instruction: What method should an IPoolable interface provide to reset state upon reuse?
q.summary: Since Awake and Start only run once upon initial creation, pooled objects use OnSpawnFromPool to reset.
q.analogy: Wiping down the chalkboard before drawing the next turn combat map.
q.memory: Resets member variables to defaults without allocating new memory.

q.speech: Spawn Boss, Flying, or Ground enemies dynamically based on dungeon level!
q.title: Factory Pattern Abstraction
q.instruction: What is the responsibility of an EnemyFactory class?
choices: Encapsulating enemy instantiation and configuration logic in one centralized class
q.summary: The Factory pattern centralizes object creation logic, decoupling spawner scripts from enemy setup details.
q.analogy: An automaker assembly plant: you ask for a sports car, and the factory handles the assembly.
q.memory: Centralized factory method routes creation parameters to correct prefab instance.

q.speech: Find the Audio service without creating 20 static singletons!
q.title: Service Locator Registry
q.instruction: How does a Service Locator provide services to game scripts?
q.code:
IAudioService audio = ServiceLocator.Get<IAudioService>();
audio.PlaySound("Victory");
choices: Scripts request services by interface type from a central registry
By hardcoding file paths on Windows
q.summary: The Service Locator pattern maintains a registry of services, allowing swappable mock services in tests.
q.analogy: Calling the hotel concierge to connect you with room service or valet parking.
q.memory: Dictionary<Type, object> lookup provides fast service reference.

q.speech: The boss enters Enrage Mode and switches from Melee to Ranged attacks!
q.title: Strategy Pattern Swapping
q.instruction: How does the Strategy Pattern allow dynamic behavior changes at runtime?
choices: The boss delegates attacks to an interchangeable strategy object that can be swapped at runtime
q.summary: The Strategy pattern defines a family of swappable algorithms, letting boss behavior vary dynamically.
q.analogy: A chess player switching from a defensive strategy to an aggressive offensive strategy.
q.memory: Swapping strategy pointer changes execution target without rebuilding GameObject.

lessons.title: Unit 9 Milestone Trial: Design Patterns Apex

q.speech: DESIGN PATTERNS BOSS! Which pattern should you combine with Object Pooling for particle effects?
q.title: Flyweight & Pool Synergy
q.instruction: What pattern shares unchanging particle geometry while Object Pooling reuses active particle instances?
q.code: // High Performance 10,000 Particle Architecture:
choices: Flyweight Pattern (shared static data) + Object Pool (instance recycling)
q.summary: The Flyweight pattern shares immutable data across instances, while Object Pooling recycles the active objects.
q.analogy: 10,000 soldiers wearing the exact same uniform design, recycled in waves.
q.memory: Minimal per-instance memory combined with zero-allocation recycling.

title: Pro Profiling, GC Optimization & Burst/Jobs
desc: Garbage collection internals, NonAlloc queries, StringBuilder, Profiler, and Burst compiler.

guidebook.summary: Master the art of 120 FPS game development, zero-allocation C#, memory profiling, and SIMD multi-threading.
tips: Physics.RaycastNonAlloc avoids generating an array on the heap every query.
Use StringBuilder instead of string concatenation in Update() loops.
Beware boxing: casting an int or struct to an object or interface creates a heap allocation.
The Unity Job System and Burst compiler compile C# into high-performance native machine code.

q.speech: Why did our mobile game stutter every 8 seconds during the boss fight?
q.title: GC Stop-The-World Spike
q.instruction: What happens when the Managed Heap runs out of room for new allocations?
choices: The Garbage Collector halts the game to scan memory and collect garbage (GC Pause)
The frame rate permanently locks at 10 FPS
q.summary: When the heap fills up, the Boehm GC halts execution to trace roots and reclaim memory, causing a visible hitch.
q.analogy: A kitchen garbage can overflowing: the chef has to stop cooking to drag the heavy bin outside.
q.memory: Traces memory graph from registers and stack roots; mark and sweep phase pause.

q.speech: Stop string garbage in Update()! Which tool creates zero-garbage formatted text?
q.title: StringBuilder Buffer
q.instruction: Why does StringBuilder prevent garbage collection churn?
choices: It modifies an internal reusable character buffer without allocating new string objects on the heap
It compresses text into ZIP format
q.summary: Strings in C# are immutable (any edit creates a brand new string). StringBuilder reuses an internal char array.
q.analogy: Using a dry-erase whiteboard instead of burning through a new notepad sheet every 16 milliseconds.
q.memory: Fixed char[] array buffer; zero garbage allocations when within pre-allocated capacity.

q.speech: Replace Physics.RaycastAll() with the zero-allocation pro version!
q.title: RaycastNonAlloc Buffer Pass
q.instruction: Why does Physics.RaycastNonAlloc produce zero heap allocations?
choices: You pass in a pre-allocated array buffer that PhysX populates in-place
It runs on the GPU raster pipeline
q.summary: RaycastAll creates a new RaycastHit[] array every call. RaycastNonAlloc populates your existing buffer for 0 bytes GC alloc.
q.analogy: Handing the cashier your own reusable shopping bag instead of buying a new plastic bag every item.
q.memory: Native PhysX writes directly into the pinned managed array pointer without heap alloc.

q.speech: HIDDEN ALLOCATION TRAP! Spot the boxing allocation in this code!
q.title: Value Type Boxing
q.instruction: What is Boxing in C#?
q.code:
int score = 100;
object boxedScore = score; // BOXING ALLOCATION!
choices: Converting a value type (int, struct) to an object or interface reference, allocating memory on the Heap
Packing items into a game loot box
q.summary: Boxing wraps a stack value inside a heap object wrapper, triggering unexpected GC allocations in game loops.
q.analogy: Wrapping an individual coin in an expensive cardboard shipping package just to hand it to a friend.
q.memory: Allocates 16-byte object header on Heap + copies value into payload; unboxing extracts value back.

q.speech: Never call GetComponent<Rigidbody>() inside Update()! What should you do instead?
q.title: Component Caching Pattern
q.instruction: What is the correct performance practice for component access?
choices: Cache the component in Awake()/Start() into a private variable
q.summary: GetComponent searches native GameObject component arrays. Caching it in Awake stores a direct pointer for O(1) access.
q.analogy: Saving your doctor phone number in your contacts instead of searching the yellow pages every time you call.
q.memory: Direct pointer dereference vs native engine component table traversal.

q.speech: Which column in the Unity Profiler hierarchy reveals hidden GC spikes?
q.title: Profiler GC Alloc Column
q.instruction: Which profiler column shows exactly how many bytes of heap memory a method allocates per frame?
q.code: // Look at Unity Profiler hierarchy:
q.summary: The GC Alloc column shows exact byte allocations per function call. In 60 FPS loops, it should read 0 B!
q.analogy: A calorie counter for your code: spotting which function is eating up the memory budget.
q.memory: Unity instrumentation tracks thread-local allocator byte counters per profile marker.

q.speech: Textures from Level 1 are still taking up 500 MB in Level 2! How do you purge them?
q.title: Unload Unused Assets
q.instruction: Which method unloads unused assets from memory after changing scenes?
q.code: Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets();
q.summary: Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets walks the native object graph and frees textures, audio, and meshes with no references.
q.analogy: Clearing out the storage room of props from the previous play that are no longer needed.
q.memory: Native C++ asset garbage collector releases GPU texture and audio buffer handles.

q.speech: Passing a 64-byte CombatData struct without copying 64 bytes on the stack!
q.title: in Parameter Passing
q.instruction: What does the "in" keyword do when passing large structs to methods in C#?
choices: Passes the struct by reference (pointer) while making it readonly, avoiding memory copying overhead
q.summary: The in modifier passes value types by reference, saving stack memory copy overhead while enforcing immutability.
